records.name: a3_duplicate_write_suppression

spec._what: A3 RECONCILED against the R9 composed incumbent. The historical population genuinely does not exist here, and the reason is a difference in HOW A1 relocates -- not a lost opportunity and not a defective reconstruction.

historical_A3.population: 59 occurrences, 100% write stage, write_rejected. ALL 59 collisions are against keys A1 ITSELF injected, verified against substitution telemetry; 54/59 = 92% carry a value token-identical to what A1 rescued.
historical_A3.chain: core fills -> A1 reroutes the write to archival under key K -> the model, UNAWARE A1 acted, later issues its own archival_memory_add(key=K, ...) -> the store answers 'Key name must be unique.'

measured_under_the_R9_incumbent.verdict: ZERO archival unique-violations across all three cells. A3's population is absent.

WHY_IT_IS_ABSENT.the_apparent_contradiction: our A1 declares destination_operation = archival_memory_add and relocated 61 times in kv, yet only ONE archival_memory_add appears in `decoded`. Those cannot both be model-issued writes.
WHY_IT_IS_ABSENT.resolved: the relocation's archival write is issued BY THE PRIMITIVE, not proposed by the model, so it never enters `decoded`. Traced: relocate_gate=61, relocate_write_result present 55 times, ALL 55 reading 'added', ZERO reading 'unique'.
WHY_IT_IS_ABSENT.consequence: the historical chain needed the MODEL to later re-issue a write for a key A1 had injected. Under this implementation the model never sees those keys in its own call history, and the 55 primitive writes land cleanly. So the collision the historical A3 suppressed is not generated at all.
WHY_IT_IS_ABSENT.this_is_an_IMPLEMENTATION_DIFFERENCE_in_: A3's opportunity is downstream of HOW A1 writes, not of whether A1 is installed. The historical A1 and this one relocate to the same destination but differ in whether the write is attributable to the model. That difference erases A3's residual.

spec.STATUS: A3 is NOT RECOVERABLE on this incumbent, and the reason is now identified rather than assumed
spec.why_this_is_not_a_silent_rejection_of_a_: The historical +3.96 pp stands as measured on ITS incumbent (N0+A1+A2 at 35.97%). What is measured here is that the residual A3 addresses is absent under A1-as-implemented-now. The honest statement is 'A3's opportunity is not generated by this A1', not 'A3 does not work'. Recovering it would require changing A1's write attribution, which would change a MEASURED controller -- a new version with its own measurement, not a tweak.
spec.supersedes: the earlier 201x projection finding, which explained the offline/live gap but left open whether the opportunity existed at all. It does not. The projection was wrong AND the residual is absent, for two independent reasons.
spec.cost_to_recover: HIGH and with a regression risk to A1, against a historical +3.96 pp. Lower priority than A5 (+1.32) despite the larger historical step, because A5 needs a new executor while A3 needs changing an accepted controller.

provenance.verdict: TRIGGER_ABSENT -- opportunity is 1 of 105, not a capability gap
provenance.why: our A1 issues relocation writes from the PRIMITIVE, so the model never re-issues a colliding key. The historical A3 population (collisions A1 itself created, re-issued by the model) does not exist here: 61 relocations, 1 archival_memory_add in decoded, 55 writes all 'added'.
provenance.projection_root_cause: the offline reconstruction builds store state from each episode's OWN writes and cannot see what the prerequisite phase already built, so absent keys look present
provenance.do_not: widen the predicate -- that would suppress writes the store does not hold

notes: reconciled, not silently rejected: the historical result stands for its own population

context.incumbent_token: arm results/kvrl_a1_train (1824859), control results/kvrl_ctl_train (1824866); held-out kvho_a1_test (1825348) vs kvho_ctl_test (1825364). Autonomously emitted by results/kv_reloc2.

notes: PRESERVATION: 58/58 relocated entries present in THEIR OWN episode's final store. RECONCILED denominators: 84 requested -> 67 verified preservations (write/removal/copy-survives/slot-freed all 67, one-to-one) -> 61 retries landed end-to-end. The earlier '61/61 write-verified' understated preservation and is corrected; see rounds/AUTONOMY/RELOCATION_CHAIN_RECONCILED.json.

29 of 58 retried keys are absent at episode end, and ALL 31 absences are explained by a later core_memory_clear issued by the AGENT -- 0 unexplained. The repair loses no information; it does not prevent the agent clearing the store afterwards.

DEV IS UNINFORMATIVE FOR TRANSFER: the kv dev split is one domain chain (customer, 24/24) and the CONTROL also scores 0/24, so criterion 2 is satisfied (net 0, no aggregate regression) but could not have shown a regression. Criterion 2 is non-regression, NOT a required gain.
SAFETY under the three-counter contract: 0 clears added, 0 information-losing removes, 61 verified relocations (bounded 3 per TURN -- see the bound caveat).
An earlier pooled-snapshot audit reporting 54/54 and 30/58 is RETRACTED; those numbers matched keys across episodes.

BOUND SCOPE CORRECTION: the primitive's MAX_RELOCATIONS_PER_EPISODE=3 is enforced by the patch against a counter declared beside _capacity_repair_fired, which the host resets inside the TURN loop (memory_evaluator.py:2198). So the bound that RAN is 3 per turn, not 3 per episode: 84 requested, 61 performed, up to 8 in one episode, 23 unserved. Preservation was verified 67/67 and 61 of those landed end-to-end (0 information-losing removes, 0 clears added); the 23 unserved requests are 16 bound-guard refusals plus 1 guard-decline, and 6 more preserved but had their retry blocked by a different constraint, so the measured result and its safety evidence stand -- but the documented bound was wrong and is corrected here rather than quietly restated. Moving the counter to episode scope would change execution semantics and require re-measurement.
